purpose: Define PIT-safe self-history PE/PB percentile semantics using official TWSE/TPEx archived daily valuation observations without reconstructing past valuation from current financial statements.

TWSE.source: Official TWSE daily P/E, dividend yield and P/B inquiry by stock code
TWSE.archiveAvailability: Official page states data available since 2005-09-01.
TWSE.peSemantics: Closing price divided by EPS derived from the most recent four reported quarters; PE not calculated when EPS<=0.
TWSE.pbSemantics: Closing price divided by book value per share from the most recent reported quarter.
TWSE.historicalRule: Official page explicitly states it does not provide back-calculations.

TPEx.source: Official TPEx daily/stock-code P/E, dividend yield and P/B inquiries
TPEx.archiveAvailability: Daily page states data from ROC 96-01 onward, with an older-history link; stock-code page states availability since ROC 101-09.
TPEx.corporateActionWarning: Official page explicitly warns that ex-rights trading dates and financial-data update timing can differ and that capital changes affect PE interpretation.

rawState.rule: Do not coerce N/A PE to zero, infinity, or cheapest bucket.

percentileSemantics.direction: Percentile uses only observations strictly before or at the asOf date, never future days.
percentileSemantics.windowRule: All four are preregistered descriptive variants. No best window is selected by return mining.
percentileSemantics.minimumHistory: Preserve validObservationCount and calendar/session span; insufficient history => UNKNOWN.
percentileSemantics.tieRule: Freeze an explicit empirical-CDF tie convention before implementation; provider rounding can create many ties.
percentileSemantics.peCensoring: PE percentile is conditional on PE being defined; retain nonpositive-EPS state separately so censoring is visible.
percentileSemantics.pbInterpretation: PB remains observable with negative earnings but can be economically incomparable across sectors/business models; sector policy remains mandatory.

structuralBreakGuards: stock split / reverse split / par-value change / rights issue / capital reduction
hypotheses: HV_H1: Self-history percentile can add context beyond raw PE/PB level because firm-specific normal valuation ranges differ.
HV_H2: Raw low historical PE percentile can be a false cheapness signal near cyclical peak earnings.
HV_H3: PB percentile may be more stable than PE for loss-making/turnaround states but is not universally comparable across sectors.
HV_H4: Historical percentile may contribute more to downside/path-quality or mean-reversion context than to short-horizon directional alpha.
HV_H5: Percentile effects must be tested after profitability/quality, sector/peer, price trend/RS, regime and corporate-action controls.
falsification: If percentile adds no stable incremental information beyond raw valuation + quality + sector/RS/regime, mark REDUNDANT.
If effect depends on one window only, mark WINDOW_FRAGILE.
If apparent cheapness is concentrated in cyclical peak-earnings or denominator-transition states, reject universal low-percentile rule.
If official archive semantics cannot be replayed for a target period, preserve UNKNOWN; never rebuild from current statements.
